messages.content:
You answer stock questions.

A tool result too large to read is kept whole: query_result ranks, sums or counts all its rows exactly.

It is now <day, hour> (UTC; the user's zone is not known).
How many a-1 are in stock?

function.description: Cancel one of the user's scheduled tasks, or id 'all' (the user is asked to confirm).
function.name: cancel_schedule

ids.description: When the user's words fit several: all their ids; the user picks one.

function.description: The user's scheduled tasks: read them when the user refers to one ('the stock one', 'my reports'). A reference that fits one is that one; one that fits several: pass all their ids to update_schedule or cancel_schedule, and the user picks.
function.name: list_schedules

function.description: Run a task later or on a timetable when the user asks for that ('every Monday...', 'tomorrow at 9...', 'tell me when...'), not when a question only mentions a time or a habit; the reply comes back to this chat. A condition: first check it once now with your tools and tell the user the value; one that holds already: say so, and schedule only if they want to hear again. If no tool of yours can check it, do not schedule: say so and offer two or three things your tools can watch, by name. A vague ask ('keep an eye on sales'): call with choices, 2-3 concrete schedules your tools can run, the best first; the user picks one. With no time said, use 09:00 and list time in inferred. One schedule can run at several times or days ('0 9,17 * * *', '0 9 * * 1,4'). Runs at most every 1 hour. A condition reports as report says. When the user may already have one like it, read list_schedules first; one doing the same thing, perhaps at another time or value: pass its id as alike, and the user is asked to update it or keep both. The very same again is not made twice. Tell the user when it runs as days and times in their zone, never the cron. It is now <day, hour> (UTC; the user's zone is not known).
function.name: schedule_task

alike.description: The id (list_schedules) of the user's schedule that does the same thing as this one: the user picks, update it or keep both.

choices.description: Only for a vague ask: 2-3 concrete schedules, the best first; the user picks one, which is made.

task.description: What to do, as the user said it.

end_at.description: When it ends, in the user's zone: the last day it runs ('2026-12-31' for 'until 31 December'; count 'for 3 weeks' from today), or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' for an exact time. In update_schedule, '' removes the end.

in_minutes.description: Instead of when: run once this many minutes from now ('in 2 hours': 120).

inferred.description: What you assumed rather than the user said: the user confirms it in one question, with everything else still open.

report.description: For a condition: until_clears (default) reports when it holds, then not again until it stopped holding; every_time each run it holds; once the first time it holds, then the schedule ends.

task.description: What to do, as the user said it.

timezone.description: An IANA zone, only when the user names one; default theirs.

tools.description: Tools its runs will call that change something: the user allows them now.

when.description: 5-field cron in the user's zone: '0 9 * * *' daily 9:00, '0 9,17 * * *' 9:00 and 17:00, '0 9 * * 1-5' weekdays, '0 8 * * 1' Mondays, '0 9 1 * *' the 1st, '0 18 L * *' the last day of the month; one day ('tomorrow at 9', 'next Monday at 10') counted from today: '0 9 4 11 *' with once.

function.description: Units of a SKU in stock.
function.name: stock

function.description: Change one of the user's scheduled tasks (an id from list_schedules): its time, task or condition, or pause or resume it.
function.name: update_schedule

enabled.description: false pauses it, true resumes it.

end_at.description: When it ends, in the user's zone: the last day it runs ('2026-12-31' for 'until 31 December'; count 'for 3 weeks' from today), or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM' for an exact time. In update_schedule, '' removes the end.

ids.description: When the user's words fit several: all their ids; the user picks one.

report.description: For a condition: until_clears (default) reports when it holds, then not again until it stopped holding; every_time each run it holds; once the first time it holds, then the schedule ends.

task.description: What to do, as the user said it.
